clue.text: Show contempt for the reportedly bamboozled in the area

parts.note: to dis someone is to show contempt for them, slang

indicators.note: reportedly says the next word is only heard, so a word that sounds like it is entered

parts.note: bamboozled means tricked, which is said like the letters TRICT

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the locals who were fooled in this neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' and 'in the' are link words; the homophone is signalled by 'reportedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a defined region or neighbourhood, a straightforward synonym for an area.

clue.text: See 22
Reaper with unhealthy bits of cell

definitions.meaning: a reaping hook, the curved blade a reaper uses to cut corn
in ...-cell anaemia the diseased red blood cells take a crescent shape

explanation.surface: A harvester accompanied by diseased fragments of a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Some solvers also see SICK (unhealthy) plus L and E, letters taken from 'cell'; the blog reads it as two definitions with the medical allusion.
explanation.definitionFit: The crescent tool used for harvesting corn, and the crescent-shaped blood cells of an inherited anaemia.

clue.text: Is that true about friend?

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letter headings
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rumour about a pal is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a question, the word is an expression of surprised doubt asking whether something is genuinely so.

clue.text: Order follows number and Bible story is like

indicators.note: follows puts the Order after the number in the answer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a parable is a story told by Jesus in the Gospels

explanation.surface: A tale from scripture resembles a command coming after a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' says OM comes after C. OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are comparable are similar enough to be compared, so one is like the other.

clue.text: Article covered by remote ancestor

indicators.note: covered by says the article sits inside the word for remote, enclosed by it

parts.note: far means distant or remote
the is the definite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concealed by a distant forebear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical article; 'covered by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is the nearest male forebear, and the word also extends to any ancestor or forefather.

clue.text: A heartless minister (solution for Saudis)

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the minister's title is taken away

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish minister of religion
ANS is a standard abbreviation of answer, that is, a solution

explanation.surface: A cruel clergyman offers an answer for the people of Saudi Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes out the central letter of the minister's title; 'solution' is the common abbreviation for answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saudis are natives of the Arabian peninsula, so they are Arabians in the broad sense of that people.

clue.text: Cordial welcome for new pastor here — unless male

indicators.note: welcome is read as the cordial word taking in, or welcoming, the letters for new and pastor

parts.note: hearty means warm and cordial
P is an abbreviation for pastor, a minister of a church

explanation.surface: A parish greets its new minister warmly, though perhaps not if he is a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcome' puts N and P inside HEARTY. The definition is a joke: this is the celebration held here, unless the guests are male, when it would be a stag party.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-wedding celebration for women; the male equivalent is a stag party, so this is the party unless it is for men.

clue.text: Antbears poisoned with arsenic

indicators.note: poisoned suggests the anteaters' letters have been disordered and corrupted

explanation.surface: South American anteaters are killed off with a toxic powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poisoned' is the anagram signal on ANTBEARS, which also suits the poison in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratsbane is an old name for rat poison, specifically arsenic used to kill rodents.

clue.text: Gets back to work miracles

indicators.note: to work means the letters of miracles are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recovers from illness so as to perform wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' rearranges MIRACLES; the surface suggests working miracles.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover it, getting it back into your possession.

clue.text: "5, I _____" give a lone cat lentil soup (21 14)

indicators.note: soup suggests the words are stirred into a mess, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A recipe gives a solitary cat a bowl of lentil broth.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 across is the parent: young George Washington (21 14) supposedly confessed to cutting down the cherry tree with these words. 'soup' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation completed reads Father, I cannot tell a lie, the confession attributed to the boy George Washington.

clue.text: … nothing but consommé then after raid?

parts.note: all means nothing but, as in all talk
consommé is a clear soup

explanation.surface: Continuing the soup theme, someone has only thin broth once the bombing ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the lentil soup of 10 across. The all-clear is the siren signal that an air raid is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is the signal sounded once danger from an air raid has passed, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Baker's vehicle kept by receiver of spills

definitions.note: a possessive standing for something belonging to a baker, here the raising agent used in baking

indicators.note: kept by says the vehicle is held inside the spill-catcher

parts.note: a bib catches what a child spills while eating
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A bread-maker's van is stored by the thing that catches drips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker's' looks like it owns the vehicle, but it is the definition: the raising agent is a baker's ingredient. 'kept by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarbonate of soda is a raising agent used in baking, so it is something of the baker's.

clue.text: Complaint about her 5 and his etc, subject of 10 27

indicators.note: about says the complaint goes round the word her

parts.note: a cry is an outcry or complaint
taken as written
5 across is father, and a father with his forebears and so on is a family tree

explanation.surface: Someone moans about her dad and his relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HER inside CRY. TREE stands for FATHER (5) and his ancestors, as on a family tree. The cherry tree is the one Washington chopped down in the story of 10 27.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree the boy Washington cut down, prompting his admission that he could not tell a lie.

clue.text: 22,1 down town in 1 across of 16

definitions.meaning: a town in the north-east of England, historically in the county named at 22 and 1 down
the federal capital of the United States, the District of Columbia

explanation.surface: A northern English town is placed in the American federal district.
explanation.walkthrough: The English town has been part of Tyne and Wear since 1974, though it was historically in County Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to a town near Sunderland and to the US capital, District of Columbia.

clue.text: I like this big hole — it links Auroral viewpoints

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
a chasm is a deep gaping hole or gorge

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a vast pit like this, which joins spots for watching the northern lights.
explanation.definitionFit: An isochasm is a map line joining places that see the aurora equally often.

clue.text: First shuttle British?

definitions.meaning: the name of the first NASA space shuttle to reach orbit, in 1981
with British in front it names the Canadian province British ...

explanation.definitionFit: The orbiter that flew the first shuttle mission, and the second word of a Canadian province's name.

clue.text: Lookout being dispatched by train?

parts.note: being dispatched means sent off
travelling by a vehicle is travelling in it
the el is an American elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A guard sent off on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: EL is short for the elevated railway of American cities such as Chicago.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or guard posted to keep watch, a lookout.

clue.text: Be unctuous without authority, sprinkling ale as precaution

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the smarming word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to smarm is to be oily and ingratiating
OK means approval or authorisation

indicators.note: sprinkling scatters the letters of ale into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fawns with no power, splashing beer about as a safety measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'sprinkling' is the anagram signal; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A device fitted as a safeguard against fire, so the definition names its purpose.

clue.text: Dependant boy or girl holding beast

indicators.note: holding says the name surrounds the animal

parts.note: Val is short for Valentine or Valerie, so a boy's or a girl's name
an ass is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A child, whether son or daughter, relies on a donkey it keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal; the name is shared by men and women, hence 'boy or girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal tenant bound to a lord, so a subordinate or dependant.

clue.text: Boy, weirdo, returning by underground route

indicators.note: returning means the boy and the weirdo are both read backwards as one run

parts.note: Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard
a nut is a crank or weirdo

explanation.surface: A lad and an oddball come back by way of the subway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses LEN + NUT, giving TUN NEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunnel is a passage dug beneath the ground, a route under the surface.

clue.text: I'll fly to 14

definitions.meaning: RAF slang name for an aircraft's automatic pilot, which flies the plane
the first name that goes before 14 across to name the first US president

explanation.surface: The speaker promises to fly to the American capital.
explanation.definitionFit: George is old RAF slang for an autopilot, and George Washington was the first US president.

clue.text: Shire shorthorn initially like 16 1 across

definitions.note: the words' initials C and D are those of Columbia and District

parts.note: a shire is a county
the Durham is the old name for the Shorthorn breed of cattle

explanation.surface: A rural county's cattle breed resembles an American district at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shorthorn cattle breed was first known as the Durham. The definition is loose: the answer's initials, C and D, match those of the District of Columbia.
explanation.definitionFit: Its two initials are the same letters as those of the District of Columbia, a playful link to the theme.

clue.text: Hear 5 charge ancient American city

indicators.note: Hear tells the solver to listen, so the words are only said aloud

parts.note: 5 across is father, or sire, and to charge is to accuse

explanation.surface: Listen as Dad accuses an old city in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' says SIRE ACCUSE is only spoken. The name is both an ancient Greek city in Sicily and a city in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Syracuse was an ancient Greek city in Sicily, and its namesake is a city in New York State.

clue.text: White man has this country's tail in a twist

indicators.note: tail in a twist means the last two letters of the country's name are turned round

parts.note: Albion is a poetic name for Britain, the setter's own country

explanation.surface: A pale man has his nation in a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail in a twist' swaps the last two letters, ON, of ALBION.
explanation.definitionFit: An albino lacks pigment, so a white man in the literal sense.

clue.text: One inside piano is one within rights

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly

indicators.note: within says the words is and one sit inside the rights

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, so two rights are RR

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument is a unit of entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One inside' is slang for a person in jail; 'within' is the container signal, and the setter reuses 'one' on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner is a person inside a jail, so 'inside' is the slang for being locked up.

clue.text: Spotted being of little consequence

definitions.meaning: covered in the spots of the disease measles

explanation.definitionFit: The word literally means suffering from measles, and colloquially means paltry or contemptibly small.
